text:
marta: Heads up — grafana alert fired: prom_remote_write_queue_backlog for prometheus-3. Lots of 'send samples failed' in logs. Appears correlated with a big cardinality spike on scrapes targeting /metrics from gpu-worker pods :

marta: log excerpt:
```
level=error ts=2026-03-18T14:12:08Z caller=remote.go:345 component=remote msg="send samples failed" err="write tcp 10.0.3.12:443: i/o timeout"
level=warn ts=2026-03-18T14:12:08Z caller=scrape.go:789 component=scrape target="http://10.1.5.23:9100/metrics" msg="append failed" num_samples=1200
```

marta: I also see a sudden explosion of unique label values for label `pod_instance_id` and `job_version` after the latest sidecar rollout. Later messages show samples/sec spiking to ~200k which overwhelmed the remote_write batcher.

sre-bot: ALERT acknowledged by @marta :white_check_mark:

devin: do we have the relabel_config for the gpu-worker job? can we drop pod_instance_id as a quick mitigation?

marta: current job snippet from prometheus config:
```
- job_name: "gpu-worker"
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: pod
  relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app]
    regex: gpu-worker
    action: keep
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_instance_id]
    target_label: pod_instance_id
```

li: yup, that annotation was added by the new sidecar; it's effectively unique per restart so cardinality is insane. Temporary fix: change action to `drop` for that source label or set `replacement: ""` and `action: replace` into `pod_instance_id` only if non-empty. Also consider adding `metric_relabel_configs` to drop high-cardinality metrics.

oscar: we rolled sidecar v2 at 13:58. It started annotating pods with `instance_hash` and `instance_seq`. Those were meant for debugging but not for prometheus. Might be a config drift.

devin: plan: 1) patch prometheus scrape relabel to drop both `pod_instance_id` and `instance_hash`; 2) reduce `scrape_interval` for gpu-worker from 15s -> 60s to throttle samples; 3) increase remote_write timeout from 30s -> 60s as a stopgap while backlog drains. Anyone opposed?

marta: sounds good. I'll apply a quick k8s patch to the prometheus-operator CR to inject relabel. Doing a dry-run first.

li: example relabel to apply (prometheus operator format):
```
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_instance_id]
  action: drop
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_instance_hash]
  action: drop
```
Also add under job `scrape_interval: 60s` and under remote_write: `timeout: 60s`

devin: remember to `promtool check config` after patch. And maybe set `max_samples_per_send` lower if available.

oscar: while that's in flight, i opened a helm rollback PR for the sidecar annotations to remove the prometheus-related ones. We should audit other jobs for accidental annotation-to-label mappings.

marta: applied patch to prometheus-operator (dry-run ok). Going to apply real now. kubectl patch cmd I used:
```
kubectl -n monitoring patch prometheus prometheus-main --type merge --patch '{"spec": {"additionalScrapeConfigs": ...}}'
```

sre-bot: deploybot: rollout started for prometheus-main config patch :rocket:

pagerduty: Incident created: INC-2026-1803 - prom_remote_write_backlog. Priority P2.

devin: after patch, backlog started to decrease. grafana shows queue length halved in ~4m. still monitoring.

marta: follow-up: we added a ticket to infra backlog to add an admission-controller check that flags high-cardinality annotations and to add a warning in the sidecar release notes. Ticket: INFRA-8742

li: long term, let's add `metric_relabel_configs` to drop labels at metric level for known problematic metrics (kube_pod_labels and app-specific exposers). Also add an alert for sudden unique label cardinality increase for a job (threshold-based).

oscar: fyi i reverted the sidecar config in helm for next release and annotated the PR with the reason.

marta: closing updates: queue is back to normal, remote_write timeouts reset to 30s, scrape_interval for gpu-worker kept at 30s for now while we implement better relabeling. leaving INFRA-8742 open. thanks all :heart:

devin: great triage. recommend a short postmortem in monday all-hands notes so product teams know why their debug annotation caused this.

marta: will draft and share.
